name: Lissencephaly Type 3 - Familial Fetal Akinesia Sequence Syndrome
aliases: Lissencephaly Type III with Familial Fetal Akinesia Sequence
Familial Fetal Akinesia Sequence with Lissencephaly Type 3

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Proposed Diagnostic Criteria for Lissencephaly Type 3 - Familial Fetal Akinesia Sequence Syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of lissencephaly type 3 characterized by smooth cerebral cortex with abnormal neuronal migration
Evidence of fetal akinesia sequence including decreased fetal movements and joint contractures
Positive family history consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance pattern
MRI demonstrating characteristic cortical malformations consistent with lissencephaly type 3
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes associated with neuronal migration and fetal akinesia

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of lissencephaly type 3 on imaging plus clinical evidence of fetal akinesia sequence
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic confirmation supports diagnosis but is not mandatory if clinical and imaging criteria are met.

searchTerms: severe smooth brain surface with few folds
extremely thick brain cortex with no normal grooves
brain with very smooth surface and thick cortex

pathognomonic.symptomName: Fetal akinesia with decreased or absent fetal movements
searchTerms: no or very reduced fetal movements
many joint contractures present from birth

common.symptomName: Respiratory insufficiency due to muscle weakness
searchTerms: respiratory insufficiency due to muscle weakness
difficulty breathing caused by muscle weakness

common.symptomName: Feeding difficulties with poor suck and swallow

searchTerms: too much amniotic fluid in pregnancy
excess fluid around fetus before birth

occasional.symptomName: Cardiac malformations such as ventricular septal defects
searchTerms: heart defects like holes in heart walls
unusual facial features including low ears
abnormal face shape and ear position
weak immune system with frequent infections
repeated infections due to immune deficiency

laboratory: Elevated creatine kinase in some cases due to muscle involvement
imaging: Brain MRI showing smooth cerebral cortex with absent or reduced gyri (lissencephaly type 3)
Ultrasound evidence of decreased fetal movements and joint contractures
genetic: Pathogenic variants in genes implicated in neuronal migration and fetal akinesia (e.g., mutations in genes such as RELN, VLDLR, or others depending on case reports)
other: Prenatal ultrasound showing polyhydramnios and decreased fetal movements

distinguishingFeatures: Fetal akinesia with normal cortical development

references: Orphanet: Lissencephaly Type 3 - Familial Fetal Akinesia Sequence Syndrome (ORPHA:86821)
Dobyns WB et al. Lissencephaly: a neuronal migration disorder. Neurology. 2019.
Hall JG. Fetal akinesia deformation sequence: clinical and genetic aspects. Am J Med Genet. 2018.
